_comment: The strangers from the map's edge in their camp at the Wide Rift (plan 2, items 141-180; docs/STORY.md 'The strangers' camp'). Root entries are '<name>'; each one switches to its closing talk once the story is complete and its own side goal is done.
arrive_say: Tents lean into the wind at the edge of the Wide Rift. Someone has hung washing on a Rift crack.
arrive_elma: Elma: Welcome to the camp of the strangers from the map's edge. Wipe your feet. On what, I couldn't tell you.
Elma: Eleven of us came through the Wide Rift. The valley counted us twice and charged us for three.
Elma: You think the fading is your problem? Our map is going blank too. We came here because there was still a here.
Elma: The guild says we're spies. Half of us are. I'd like to know which half before they do.
Elma: Stay, help, and keep your purse on the inside of your coat. Even around me. Especially around me.

lines: Elma: The Rift stays how it stays. We stay how we stay. Mostly in debt.
Elma: Mirela and I learned to draw at the same table, you know. She always smudged the coastlines.
Elma: Still does. From the inside. Tell her the soup's on, if you see her.
Elma: All eleven of us owe you something. That has never happened. It's frightening.
Elma: This one came through the Rift with us. It draws maps of places it has never been. Ours, mostly.
Elma: Its last keeper sold us out at the border. It remembered. It bit him. Be nice to it.
Elma: Since you're standing there being useful-looking: the camp needs three things.
Elma: Fire for the pot, water for the barrel and something heavy to sit on the tent pegs.
Elma: An Ember Spirling, a Tide one and a Stone one. Show me and I'll put them to work. Paid in soup.
Elma: An Ember one! Light the cookfire. Careful, the last cook lit himself.
Elma: He's fine. Eyebrows are optional where we come from.
Elma: Fill the barrel, little one. Rift water tastes of Tuesday. Don't ask which Tuesday.
Elma: Sit on the tent pegs, would you? Last storm we lost two tents and a husband.
Elma: The tents were new.
Elma: Fire, water, pegs. You've done more for this camp than the whole valley. Low bar. You cleared it.
Elma: Still waiting on fire from an Ember Spirling, water from a Tide one and a Stone one for the pegs.

elma_chat: Elma: Eleven of us came. Count us now and then. If the number changes, tell me before you tell the guild.
Elma: Help every one of us and I'll give you something from the other map. It only bites people it doesn't know.

lines: Aldra: Two maps, one edge, and you walked both. I'll draw you in.
Aldra: Small. Near the margin. Where the interesting people go.
Aldra: Our map and yours share an edge. I'd like to know if they share a lie too.
Aldra: Take my copy to the guild in Madderby and lay it on their survey table.
Aldra: If anyone asks, you drew it. Badly.
Aldra: Same coastline. Same burned-out spot in the middle. On both maps?
Aldra: Someone on each side scratched out the same place. That's not a mistake. That's an agreement.
Aldra: Here's the true copy. The one I sold Fenrick has the rivers running backwards.
Aldra: He'll drown with total confidence.
Aldra: I'd give you the true copy, but I sold it this morning. Fenrick paid well.
Aldra: Have these. Call it a conscience. A small one, I'm still breaking it in.
Aldra: The survey table in the Madderby guild house. Lay my copy on it. Don't let anyone fold it into a crane.

aldra_chat: Aldra: I draw borders for a living. Nobody has ever thanked a border.

lines: You unfold Aldra's copy next to the guild's map.
The coastlines match. So does a burned-out patch in the middle. Someone scratched out the same place on both maps.
Amir: Heider brought me tea this morning. I didn't drink it.
Amir: Family is about trust. And also about not drinking the tea.
Amir: My family crossed before me. We agreed on a mark: a circle with a crack through it.
Amir: Look for it. The Greyreach first, then wherever the road goes after.
Amir: They'll have kept walking. We're good at walking. Bad at arriving.
Amir: All three marks. And the last one is fresh. Someone from this camp drew it.
Amir: That's my brother's hand. Heider. He sold my family's crossing places to both clans, one mark at a time.
Amir: I'm not angry. I'm counting. When I've finished counting, I'll be angry.
Amir: A circle with a crack through it. The Greyreach first. Then further, as the road opens.

amir_chat: Amir: I hatch eggs for a living. You learn patience. And which ones to drop.

lines: A circle with a crack through it, chalked on a stone.
Under it, small: 'Went on. Don't trust the eggs.'
Another cracked circle, scratched into the salt crust.
Under it: 'Still walking. Your brother says hello.'
The cracked circle again, on the well stone. This one is fresh.
The chalk is the blue kind Heider sells. Nobody else in Solenne has any.

amir_mark_wait: A circle with a crack through it. Someone drew it in a hurry.

lines: Farida: Grell stopped paying. Nobody cares who sleeps where once the world stops ending.
Farida: Shame. I was good at it.
Farida: Rest stop. Free beds, free soup, free advice. The advice is worth what you pay.
Farida: Lie down. I'll watch your things. Watching is what I do best.
Farida: You read my guest book. Rude. Accurate, but rude.
Farida: Grell pays by the name. Yours fetched a good price. You should be flattered.

farida_burn: Farida: Grell will just ask me to remember it. I have a terrible memory. For a price, it improves.
farida_lie: Farida: Lies? I'll write lovely lies. 'Travels alone. Afraid of ducks.' Grell will believe the ducks.

lines: Farida: My guest book is by the water barrel. Don't read it. Everyone reads it.

farida_chat: Farida: I patch up Spirlings and I patch up stories. Same needle.

lines: Farida's guest book. Every guest, every night, and which way they walked in the morning.
Your name is in it. Next to it: 'Snores. Trusts people. Worth 40 coins to Grell.'

ledger_farida_book: Farida's guest book: she sells every camp guest's name to Mother Grell.
You burned your page. Grell now knows you burn pages.

lines: Heider: Peace is terrible for business. I sell souvenirs of the feud now.
Heider: Mostly to the people who started it.
Heider: Wares from the far map. Everything is genuine. Genuinely from somewhere else.
Heider: Errand for you. Carry this crate to the trail post in the Greyreach. Don't shake it.
Heider: Don't open it either. Opening it voids the warranty. And possibly you.
Heider: Delivered? Then you've met my buyers. Lovely people. Terrible losers.
Heider: Your cut. I sold them your route as well, but I'm giving you the money for it. That's practically loyalty.
Heider: The crate. The Greyreach. The trail post. I'll wait. Waiting is free, unlike everything else.

heider_chat: Heider: News, wares, people. I sell what's in demand. Right now that's you.

lines: You set Heider's crate down by the trail post. Something inside ticks like a pocket watch.
Two figures step out of the scree. They knew exactly when you would come.

heider_buyers_defeat: Buyer: Heider said you'd come alone and tired. He was half right. He's always half right.

lines: Kenan: Remember me? I borrowed your Spirling once. Or someone's. They all look alike when they're asleep.
Kenan: Fight me. I win, you forget the keepsake. You win, I forget I ever took it. Fair?
Kenan: Round two. I've been training. Mostly running away, but faster.
Kenan: Rematch when my Spirlings have grown. And my excuses. Next act, as the bards say.
Kenan: Last round. If I lose, I'll tell you where the keepsake is. If I win, I'll tell you anyway, but smugly.
Kenan: One more round, once the road south is open. I'll be here. Nobody else will have me.
Kenan: Three times. Fine. Your keepsake was in Nail's tea tin all along. Nail doesn't know. Nail never knows.
Kenan: It's a bit stained. Everything in that tin is.
Kenan: The world didn't end. Shame, I'd sold tickets.
Kenan: One more for old times? I've got nothing left to steal from you, so this one's honest.

kenan_chat: Kenan: I run the Rift for whoever pays. Today that's nobody. I'm running for fun. It's awful.
kenan_d1_defeat: Kenan: Fine. Forgotten. What were we talking about? See, it works.
kenan_d2_defeat: Kenan: You've got worse at losing. That was a compliment. I think.
kenan_d3_defeat: Kenan: Three for three. I'd be ashamed if I knew how.
kenan_rematch_defeat: Kenan: Honest losing. Never tried it before. Zero stars.

lines: Leith: Nobody sends me anywhere any more. I go for walks.
Leith: Nobody's waiting at the end. It's strange. I think I like it.
Leith: Sable's done with me. Funny. So was everyone before her.
Leith: I know a hidden way to an old Warden stash at the far end of the Wide Rift. Chalk arrow, can't miss it.
Leith: It's real this time. Probably. Depends how much you trusted me back then.
Leith: You came back. So either it was the real path, or you're tougher than Sable's lot.
Leith: Either way I'm impressed. Here. I was saving it for my own escape.
Leith: Far end of the Wide Rift. Chalk arrow. Go before I change my mind about which way it points.

leith_chat: Leith: I run messages. I don't read them. That's a lie, but a professional one.

lines: Leith's chalk arrow points at a loose slab. Under it: an old Warden stash, untouched.
Leith's chalk arrow points at a loose slab. Under it: nothing.
Behind you: Sable's hands. Old orders travel slowly.

leith_trap_defeat: Sable's hand: Leith sent us this map a year ago. Never said it was cancelled.

lines: Lejla: I forged a peace treaty last night, just to see how it looks.
Lejla: It looks nice. Someone should sign a real one.
Lejla: I forge papers, and I sing while I do it. The papers come out more convincing.
Lejla: There's a stone guard by the Rift that hasn't said a word in a hundred years. My song could wake it.
Lejla: But the wind eats my voice. Bring a Gale Spirling to carry the tune.
Lejla sings. Your Spirling catches the tune and throws it at the Rift.
Lejla: Hear that? The stone is humming back. Go and say hello. Politely. It hasn't forgiven anyone in a century.
Lejla: It woke, it fought, it went back to sleep. Like my uncle at weddings.
Lejla: Here, a copy of its old Warden pass. My copy is better than the original.
Lejla: A Gale Spirling for the tune, then the stone guard up by the Rift.

lejla_chat: Lejla: Liss still sends me letters to copy. I copy them faithfully. Then I copy them for you.

lines: The stone guard opens one eye. Then the other. Then a third one you didn't know about.
It hums Lejla's tune, badly, and attacks.

silent_warden_defeat: The stone guard nods once, slowly, and goes back to being a stone.

lines: Lipka: I'm ten now! I've stopped selling tips. I sell maps.
Lipka: They're mostly wrong. That's the fun part.
Lipka: Don't tell anyone, but there's a hurt Spirling in that crate. Found it at the Rift. It bit me. We're friends now.
Lipka: It needs Waking Moss. I'd buy some, but nobody sells to me twice.
Lipka: Moss! Give it here. Hold its head. No, the other end.
Lipka: It's up! It's flapping! It's... leaving. Bye! Ungrateful. I love it.
Lipka: It left this behind. A keepsake, I think. Or it was sick on it. Either way, yours.
Lipka: It's better! So I sold it to Heider. He gave me a good price. It gave him a good bite.
Lipka: Half the money's yours. Partners. Don't look at me like that, I'm nine.
Lipka: One Waking Moss. Please. I'll owe you. I'm good for it. Ask anyone. Actually, don't ask anyone.

lipka_chat: Lipka: New tip, free: never trust a kid who sells tips.

lines: Mirza: I won my last game and stopped.
Mirza: Winning is boring when you don't have to.
Mirza: I play cards at night and hammer charms by day. Both need steady hands and no conscience.
Mirza: Bring me a Kin Charm. I'll beat it into something that holds a bond like a debt holds a family.
Mirza: Give it here. Don't watch my hands.
Mirza: Done. A charm that brightens a Spark. Don't tell Sable. She thinks I only cheat at cards.
Mirza: Funny story. I bet your charm last night and lost it.
Mirza: Won two others back, though. From a man who cried. Here.
Mirza: One Kin Charm. I'll make it better. Or lose it at cards. Usually the first.

mirza_chat: Mirza: The card hall burned down. I didn't do it. I was paid not to stop it. Different thing.

lines: Nail: Veit came by. He bought tea. Paid in coins, not promises.
Nail: People change. Tea helps.
Nail: Tea? It's free now. Someone else pays me to be nice to you.
Nail: Veit Harrow. He wants to know how strong you are. I said I'd find out. With tea.
Nail: Or you beat me, I tell him you're terrifying, and he stays away from my stall. I prefer that one.
Nail: Ready to terrify me?
Nail: I'll tell Veit you flattened me. Which you did. Nice when lying and the truth agree.
Nail: I'm done working for him. He pays in promises, and I can't brew those.

nail_chat: Nail: Tea's on the house. The house is a tent. Mind the house.
nail_duel_defeat: Nail: Terrifying. I'll write that down for Veit. Underlined.
